metadata.indicator_name: Total Annual Gross Domestic Product (GDP) at constant prices in dolllars
metadata.definition:
The Gross Domestic Product (GDP) in constant prices/ volume terms is the value of the flow of goods and services in a country at market prices for a base year, in this case 2018, which reflects the changes only due to volume variation, isolating those due to price changes. The figures are in United States dollars, utilizing the exchange rate rf corresponding to the year 2018 published by the International Monetary Fund (IMF).
Regional and subregional totals are based on available data for the countries of the region.
metadata.calculation_methodology:
The national accounts for the region at constant 2018 prices are obtained by back-casting and forward-extrapolating the current values of that year using the volume indices of the GDP components, calculated from the official series in national currency and applied both to the total and to each major ISIC division.

2018 is used as the base year; from there, each component is moved forward and backward according to its own volume index, which makes it possible to isolate real growth in activity from the effects of price changes.

The issue is that these indices are calculated and applied independently for total GDP and for each major ISIC division. Since the real growth of each sector doesn't necessarily move in the same proportion as the aggregate, the sum of the sectors at constant prices doesn't exactly match the total GDP obtained independently. That difference is the statistical discrepancy, and rather than forcing it to zero or distributing it arbitrarily across sectors, it's reported as a separate line in the corresponding table, following standard practice in fixed constant-price, base-year national accounts systems.
